chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from al-Washa', from Aban, from Hariz, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Take a prayer place in your house. So whenever you fear something, wear two thick garments from the thickest of your clothes, and pray in them. Then kneel on your knees, cry out to Allah, ask Him for Paradise, and seek refuge with Allah from the evil of that which you fear. And beware that Allah does not hear from you a word of rebellion, even if you are pleased with yourself and your clan.

key_terms.اجْثُ عَلَى رُكْبَتَيْكَ: Kneel on your knees (a specific posture of supplication)
key_terms.كَلِمَةَ بَغْيٍ: A word of rebellion / arrogance / pride
key_terms.مَسْجِدٌ: A place of prostration/prayer, specifically a dedicated spot in the home

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended prayer ritual for seeking refuge from fear according to Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him)?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi outlines the ritual of Salat al-Khawf (Prayer of Fear), emphasizing the physical posture of humility—kneeling and crying out—as a means to seek divine protection from specific threats. Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) links this external act of worship to internal spiritual integrity, warning against the corruption of pride (kibr) in one's self or lineage, which can invalidate the sincerity of the supplication. This practice reflects the Shia emphasis on utilizing domestic spaces for spiritual resilience and maintaining a balance between fear of Allah and hope in His mercy.

en.hubeali:
Al-Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moalla Bin Muhammad, from Al-Washa, from Aban, from Hareyz, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Take a Masjid to be in your house. So whenever you fear something, wear two thick clothes, from the thickest of your clothes, and pray Salāt in these two. Then leap upon your knees and shriek to Allahazwj, and ask Himazwj for the Paradise, and seek Refuge with Allahazwj from the evil of that which you fear. And beware of Having Allahazwj to hear from you rebellious words even though you may feel very proud of yourself or your tribe’.
en.sarwar: 2. Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad has narrated from Mu‘alla’ ibn Muhammad from al-Washsha’ from Aban from Hariz who has said the following: “Abu ’Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said

to assign a place in your home as Masjid. If something frightens you, dress in two pieces of your roughest clothes and perform Salah (prayer) with them. Thereafter rise on your knees and call for help, scream before Allah, ask Him for paradise, beg Him for protection against whatever has frightened you. Beware of having Allah to hear from you rebellious words even though You may feel very proud of yourself or your tribe.”
